CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 62-year-old male with past medical history significant for type I diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with complaints of shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient reports noticing some swelling, which he attributes to dietary indiscretion including salty foods consumed at house parties. He feels lethargic. Dyspnea is exertional, occurring with walking up stairs. Patient denies dyspnea at rest while sitting. He reports mild leg swelling. Patient endorses mild morning stiffness and discomfort when lying flat in bed. He reports one episode of acute nocturnal dyspnea approximately one week ago that has not recurred. Blood sugars have been well-controlled on insulin pump, though patient admits to less frequent monitoring on weekends. Regarding depression, patient reports a difficult year and a half but has not been on medications; has tried natural solutions including outdoor stretches. Reflux managed with lifestyle modifications including reduced caffeine and red bull intake and limited alcohol, particularly during holiday season. Patient denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorsed shortness of breath on review of systems sheet completed at check-in. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type I diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, reflux.

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump for type I diabetes, omeprazole 20 milligrams daily for reflux.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient consumes chocolate bars regularly. Consumes caffeine and red bull, which he has been cutting back on. Alcohol intake reduced, particularly during holiday season. Works during the week and reports being very busy on weekends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Pulse oximetry normal. Neck exam: No jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits. Cardiac exam: 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated. Pulmonary exam: Crackles bilaterally at the bases. Lower extremity exam: 1+ pitting edema.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease. Labs: White blood cell count not elevated, no evidence of pneumonia.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Shortness of breath/acute heart failure exacerbation: Start lasix 40 milligrams daily. Patient instructed to weigh himself daily and call if weight is not decreasing or if increasing. Instructed to call or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest or if acute dyspnea develops, as may require intravenous diuretics.
2. Type I diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c in approximately one month to assess need for adjustments. Patient to follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam completed.
3. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications started at this time.
4. Reflux: Continue omeprazole 20 milligrams daily.
